# AI Collaboration Log

This file documents how I used an AI assistant (Google Antigravity) to complete
the charting task in Section 3 of the assessment.

---

## 1. Initial Prompt

I asked the AI assistant:

> "Write a Python script using Matplotlib to read `output_summary.json` and create
> a bar chart comparing the average temperature of each device. Save the chart as
> `temperature_summary.png`."

**First version generated by the AI:**

```python
import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

with open("output_summary.json", "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

devices = list(data.keys())
temperatures = [data[dev]["average_temperature"] for dev in devices]

plt.bar(devices, temperatures)
plt.title("Average Temperature per Device")
plt.savefig("chart.png")
plt.show()
```

---

## 2. Issue in the Initial Version

The first version had no value labels above the bars and no axis labels. Without
labels it was hard to read exact temperatures at a glance, and there was no axis
title explaining the unit. The output filename was also `chart.png` instead of
`temperature_summary.png` as requested.

---

## Note on NaN handling (Section 1 and 2)

While testing `sanitizer.py` with edge-case inputs, I found that `float('nan')`
passes Python's `float()` conversion without raising an error, but `nan`
comparisons always return `False` — so NaN values would silently pass through
all the filters and end up in the output list. The same issue applies if a CSV
row contains the string `"nan"` as a temperature value.

A `math.isfinite()` check was added in both `sanitizer.py` and `summarizer.py`
to explicitly drop these values.
